E-field analysis stroke TMS

Diego Arias, PhD

2026-09-15

Because e-field estimates are very small when using a di/dt=1 A/us, the output is scaled. TMS simulations considered the use of the cool-B65 AP coil.

scale_factor = 1.2*(150/2) # di/dt at MSO for cool-B65 AP coil
sub_data_all.df$avg_roi_E_magn_sc <- sub_data_all.df$avg_roi_E_magn*scale_factor
sub_data_all.df$avg_roi_E_normal_sc <- sub_data_all.df$avg_roi_E_normal*scale_factor
sub_data_all.df$p99_9_sc <- sub_data_all.df$p99_9*scale_factor

sub_data_all.df$age_c <-scale(sub_data_all.df$age,
                              center = TRUE,
                              scale = FALSE)

# also we substract the average from the age for interpretability of the model.

Stats analyses

1 - Avg. E-field magnitude

a) Linear mixed-effect model

mod1 <- lmer(avg_roi_E_magn_sc ~
               #Fixed Effects
               FS*grp_age +
               #Random Effects
               (1|subID),
               #Define the data:
               data=sub_data_all.df, REML = TRUE)

summary(mod1)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: avg_roi_E_magn_sc ~ FS * grp_age + (1 | subID)
##    Data: sub_data_all.df
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 324.4
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -1.90742 -0.36384  0.00109  0.31887  2.32000 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  subID    (Intercept) 41.102   6.411   
##  Residual              2.013   1.419   
## Number of obs: 62, groups:  subID, 31
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                 Estimate Std. Error      df t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)      42.3788     1.6415 30.3855  25.817  < 2e-16 ***
## FSon             -2.3742     0.5016 29.0000  -4.733 5.32e-05 ***
## grp_ageYNG       -0.7539     2.3599 30.3855  -0.319    0.752    
## FSon:grp_ageYNG  -0.1212     0.7211 29.0000  -0.168    0.868    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) FSon   gr_YNG
## FSon        -0.153              
## grp_ageYNG  -0.696  0.106       
## FSn:grp_YNG  0.106 -0.696 -0.153

b) Stats report

report(mod1)
## We fitted a linear mixed model (estimated using REML and nloptwrap optimizer)
## to predict avg_roi_E_magn_sc with FS and grp_age (formula: avg_roi_E_magn_sc ~
## FS * grp_age). The model included subID as random effect (formula: ~1 | subID).
## The model's total explanatory power is substantial (conditional R2 = 0.96) and
## the part related to the fixed effects alone (marginal R2) is of 0.04. The
## model's intercept, corresponding to FS = off and grp_age = OLD, is at 42.38
## (95% CI [39.09, 45.67], t(56) = 25.82, p < .001). Within this model:
## 
##   - The effect of FS [on] is statistically significant and negative (beta =
## -2.37, 95% CI [-3.38, -1.37], t(56) = -4.73, p < .001; Std. beta = -0.36, 95%
## CI [-0.52, -0.21])
##   - The effect of grp age [YNG] is statistically non-significant and negative
## (beta = -0.75, 95% CI [-5.48, 3.97], t(56) = -0.32, p = 0.751; Std. beta =
## -0.12, 95% CI [-0.84, 0.61])
##   - The effect of FS [on] × grp age [YNG] is statistically non-significant and
## negative (beta = -0.12, 95% CI [-1.57, 1.32], t(56) = -0.17, p = 0.867; Std.
## beta = -0.02, 95% CI [-0.24, 0.20])
## 
## Standardized parameters were obtained by fitting the model on a standardized
## version of the dataset. 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) and p-values were
## computed using a Wald t-distribution approximation.

c) Violin plot
